summary: Executed the full upgrade regression covering Consent Guard, WhatsApp simulation, Webhook simulate (STOP-on-opt-out + stop-on-reply), Campaign Studio lifecycle (approval-gated), Follow-up Autopilot (seconds-based, stop-on-opt-out), Developer API keys (create-once, list-masked, scope enforcement, rotate, revoke, agent 403), Analytics shape, Tenant Isolation (fresh workspace + cross-tenant read block + API-key scoping), No secret leakage (WhatsApp connection GET, audit log, dev-key listing) and AI Poster (real GPT Image 1 generation + PNG serving) + Brand profile. 26/26 backend pytest tests PASS. Frontend smoke: login OK; /consent, /campaigns, /ai-studio, /developer, /analytics, /whatsapp, /automations all render without crashes; new-campaign-btn, campaign-name, campaign-message, create-campaign-btn, create-key-btn data-testids all present.

issues: React console warning: useEffect body is async function returning a Promise. Should be refactored to define+call an inner async fn inside useEffect. Non-blocking but noisy in console.

action_items: (Optional/low) Refactor useEffect(async ...) in Campaigns.js and Developer.js to inner-async pattern to silence React warning.

(Optional/low) Consider clearing/updating opt_out_registry entry when POST /api/consent/leads/{id} re-grants consent — currently registry entry with channel=null persists and would block a re-opted-in lead sharing the same phone_hash. Not observed as a functional bug in specced flows but worth a note.
critical_code_review_comments: consent.can_send() is the single hard gate and is correctly invoked from whatsapp.send_via_channel, studio.send, autopilot._run_due, and preview. No bypass path detected.

core._redact() in audit only redacts keys matching token|secret|password|api_key|access — audit stores meta with 'phone_number_id'/'waba_id' which are non-secret identifiers; verified access_token and app_secret never persisted in plaintext (encrypted via Fernet) and never returned in GET /whatsapp/connection.
devapi stores only sha256 hash of API keys; list endpoint returns prefix only; rotate/revoke invalidate old keys correctly (verified by test).
autopilot_loop() runs every 15s and correctly enforces STOP conditions (opted_out, campaign_paused, replied, converted) before send.
Tenant isolation verified: every query is scoped by workspace_id, X-API-Key context.workspace_id is enforced on all /api/v1 endpoints.
server.py still ~950 lines all-in-one for the legacy API; new modules are properly split. Consider splitting server.py later.
llm_text uses hard-coded model 'gpt-5.4'; poster uses gpt-image-1 correctly.

success_rate.frontend: 100% smoke (all upgrade pages render, key data-testids present)

test_credentials: demo@gold-e.ai / demo1234 (owner), priya@gold-e.ai / agent1234 (agent) — both work as documented.
seed_data_creation: Tests create TEST_/uuid-prefixed leads, campaigns, dev API keys, follow-ups and a second workspace (WS_B_*). Poster test also creates one generated_asset. Workspace policy frequency_limit was left at 9999 in demo workspace at end of run to avoid flakiness; main agent can reset via PUT /api/consent/policy if desired.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full upgrade regression at /app/backend/tests/test_upgrade.py — run with: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_upgrade.py -v. Deselect TestPoster with --deselect .../TestPoster for a fast <45s pass; include it (~15s more) to also cover real GPT Image 1. The autopilot test sleeps ~22s to wait for the in-process 15s scheduler tick. Legacy regression from iteration_1 (/app/backend/tests/test_backend.py) is still valid.
rca of the issue: No blocking issues. Two initial test failures during suite authoring were caused by (a) frequency-limit accumulation across test runs — fixed by bumping policy to 9999 inside the test; (b) opt_out_registry entry keyed on phone_hash surviving across test runs and blocking a newly-created lead that reused a phone number — fixed by randomising phone per fixture. These uncovered a real design note: re-granting consent via POST /api/consent/leads/{id} does NOT clear the opt-out registry entry; if the same phone_hash is re-used the lead remains blocked. Not a functional bug in the specced flows but worth flagging.
